text:
maria: quick q — we're seeing users confused in the console when they hit degraded routes vs explicit throttles. the console just shows "error" and the SDK surfaces a 429 in both cases. can we standardize the surface so client teams can decide retry/backoff properly?

tyler: agree. current ambiguity comes from us mapping both conditions to the same internal status bucket before we pick an http code. we then map to 429 for both. that's bad for consumer logic.

ajay: are the two cases: (1) queue full / quota exceeded (true throttle) and (2) route fallback where we serve a cheaper model or reduced tokens (degrade)?

maria: exactly. degrade is still "served" but lower Q, throttle is a real deny. both look like 429 right now.

lisa: quick telemetry note — dashboards currently tag these with route_result:fail but we don't distinguish fail_mode. i've had to manually filter traces to tell them apart.

ben: suggestion: expose a compact header and telemetry tag. e.g. header: `x-rw-fail-mode: throttle|degrade|fallback` and telemetry label `fail_mode` with same values. client sdk can then interpret.

tyler: love that. also add a `x-rw-reason` short subcode for more detail (quota, capacity, model_unavailable, cf). sample: `x-rw-fail-mode: degrade
x-rw-reason: model_quantized_fallback`

ajay: implementation-wise, runtime already knows the decision point. cheap to plumb these fields out of the router. impact: minor perf on header write but negligible.

sre-oncall: important: we should keep HTTP semantics sane. degrade should be 200 (or 206?) since we're returning valid output; throttle should be 429. we must not start returning 200 for throttled-deny.

maria: agreed. proposal:
- throttle => 429 + `x-rw-fail-mode: throttle`
- degrade/fallback => 200 + `x-rw-fail-mode: degrade|fallback` and `x-rw-quality: low|med|high` optional
- deny (quota hard limit) => 403 + `x-rw-fail-mode: deny`

lisa: console UX: map fail_mode to the badge color and help text. `throttle` -> red pill + tooltip "rate-limited; retry with backoff"; `degrade`/`fallback` -> amber pill + tooltip "served lower-quality model; see runbook". That will cut down support tickets.

ben: telemetry: emit metric `requests.fail_mode.[throttle|degrade|deny|ok]` and tag spans with `fail_mode`. also add sampling for degraded responses so we can run quality evals automatically.

maria: any objections? if none i'll open RFC and a small runtime PR.

tyler: nit: for streaming responses where we switch models mid-stream, we should set header immediately when decision made and update telemetry if the final state changes. otherwise clients get stale info.

sre-oncall: add a rollout plan: gate the header behind flag `rw.fail_mode_headers_v1` for 2 weeks, auto-collect errors, and rollback if we see client complaints. also add a datapoint in the incident dashboard for user-facing errors.

ajay: i'll own the runtime PR to add headers + span tag. i'll add tests for idempotency and ensure no extra payload on the wire.

lisa: i'll update console badge mapping and tooltip copy. also add a quick help doc linking to runbook and SDK guidance (how to treat 200+degrade vs 429).

ben: i'll wire metrics in observability infra and add `fail_mode` to the per-route dashboard.

maria: deploy-bot: schedule canary for flag `rw.fail_mode_headers_v1` starting tmrw at 10:00 PT to 5% traffic?

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: flag=rw.fail_mode_headers_v1, window=2024-06-12T17:00:00Z..2024-06-12T21:00:00Z, rollout=5% -> 20% pending.

maria: perfect. action items: RFC+PRs: ajay/runtime, lisa/console, ben/obs. i'll draft RFC tonight and ping infra for SLO/telemetry checks. thanks all :thumbsup:
